result.title: ReMiC: Representation-Driven Token Pruning for 3D VLMs via Minimax Hierarchical Clustering
result.summary: 3D vision-language models (3D VLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in 3D scene understanding and spatial reasoning. However, their reliance on multi-view inputs produces long visual token sequences, imposing substantial computational overhead during inference. Existing pruning methods often rely on token salience or feature diversity as proxies for representativeness, without explicitly modeling the representation gap between the original token set and the retained subset, thereby leading to suboptimal representation of the original scene. In this paper, we propose ReMiC, a training-free, representation-driven token pruning framework based on minimax hierarchical clustering. ReMiC treats retained tokens as prototypes for the original observations, formulating pruning as minimizing the maximum representation error under a fixed token budget. Local prototype initialization allocates tokens according to regional representation needs, while global prototype refinement updates the selected prototypes using cross-region information to further reduce the maximum representation error. Extensive experiments conducted on three representative 3D VLMs across five 3D scene understanding benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization of our method. Notably, by retaining only 10% of visual tokens, ReMiC preserves 93.2% of the performance of Video-3D LLM and achieves a $2.04\times$ faster inference speed.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ReMiC，一个免训练的 3D VLM 视觉 token 剪枝框架：以 minimax 层次聚类把保留 token 当作原始观测的原型，在固定 token 预算下最小化最大表示误差，并用局部原型初始化与全局原型精炼分配预算。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用原型最小化最大表示误差」的度量方式可能可供核查如何量化视觉证据压缩后的信息损失与代表性 token 选择，但该方法是静态输入剪枝，不涉及推理期 latent 状态生成或使用。
